correctness.rationale: At a₀=1/(2d), write a=a₀+cb² and F=x+1/2+b h(x)+b² k(x)+O(b³), where h=(Ω/d)sin(2πx), k=dc−a₀sin²(2πx). Then h(x+1/2)=−h(x) and k(x+1/2)=k(x), so the second iterate has coefficient 2k−hh′, namely 2dc−a₀+a₀cos(4πx)−π(Ω/d)²sin(4πx). The remainder is uniform in C² on bounded c and compact Ω ranges with d>0. For small b, g(x)=1−(Ω−b sin(2πx))² is positive and F′>0 on the relevant parameter strip. In fact ∂ₐF²(x)=g(F(x))+F′(F(x))g(x)>0. Thus there is a unique periodic profile a=𝒜_b(x) (inside (0,1) at fixed |Ω|<Ω_c by uniform bracketing), analytic even through b=0 before selecting extrema, with 𝒜_b−a₀ divisible by b². Its scaled profile tends in C² to the single frequency-2 harmonic plus a constant; its four simple critical points persist with no additional ones. The map x↦F_{𝒜_b(x)}(x) is C¹-close to a half-turn, preserves the profile and pairs the two maxima and the two minima; a regular level therefore gives precisely two primitive orbits. Since ∂ₓ(F²−x−1)=−∂ₐ(F²−x−1)𝒜_b′ along the profile, signs give one attracting and one repelling orbit, while at extrema the second derivative is nonzero and ∂ₐ(F²−x−1)>0, giving nondegenerate saddle-nodes. Half-turn conjugacy under b↦−b makes the analytic extreme values even, so the remainder is O(b⁴). For Ω=0, G=F−1/2 is increasing and G²=F²−1; G²(x)=x iff G(x)=x. The increment range gives the exact symmetric interval. Near Ω_c the same profile extends through the cap; ∂_Ω a₀(Ω_c)=2√2, which gives the stated unique local cap edge and its coefficient (√(1+4π²)−1)/(2√2). At the edge only the lower endpoint is admissible. Inspected the frozen verification and numerical script without running it. The analytic comparison controls the all-orbit count and uniformity, not a grid search.

value.rationale: The two contributions to the resonance have the same perturbative order and affect the lower and upper edges differently. The width and complete local census are quantitative results for a studied map, and the strictly positive cap shift shows that small coupling permits locking in a region forbidden at zero coupling. The cap is a pre-existing model constraint, not a slice chosen merely to get a solvable example.
